transcript:
Header: 2026-11-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 75 mins | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SRE), Dana (HelixAI ML Eng), Luis (HelixAI Infra), Rachel (HelixAI CTO)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, quick intro then hand to Priya for the deep dive
[00:07] Dana: thanks Alex, Dana here, we'll keep the agenda tight, we mostly want perf numbers and tradeoffs for on-prem
[00:12] Priya: cool, i'll run through runtime, batching, kv cache, quantization notes and then we can get into MoE and rope scaling, sorry for any background noise
[00:20] Luis: no worries, curious about routing costs for our MoE experiments, we're seeing big spikes
[00:26] Priya: yeah MoE routing is the big wildcard - activation sparsity helps but per-token routing overhead and memory pressure keep popping up, we'll show numbers
[00:35] [00:45] Marco: quick note on infra, for on-prem we need to nail down NIC/RDMA config and KMS access through peering
[00:52] Rachel: we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem, security and predictable latency are top, cost second

--- Summary / Topics ---
[05:10] Priya: first slide, Llama 2 style models, Mistral medium and Qwen families. For dense models with standard attention we recommend continuous batching with dynamic latency budgets; for qwen large sequences we suggest custom kernel selection.
[06:05] Dana: when you say continuous batching, what's the latency hit at p50 vs p95?
[06:12] Priya: good question, typical p50 for a small prompt (128 tokens) on a 80GB A100 equiv is 40-60ms with batching enabled up to batch size 8; p95 goes to 120-180ms depending on kv cache hit rate and tokenization overhead, but if you lower the latency SLO we can cap batch window to 20ms which reduces throughput but keeps p95 ~90-110ms
[07:05] Luis: our peak qps is 600 and we need p95 < 200ms, seems tight
[07:12] Alex: that's where dedicated pools and routing policies help; also cache warmup matters

[12:30] Priya: KV cache - we prefer host-side pinned memory for 1st hop and gpu-resident cache for hot sessions. For Mistral smaller kv entries let us fit more in GPU memory; for Llama 70B kv size grows and we do aggressive eviction heuristics
[13:05] Dana: eviction heuristics, can you control per-customer TTLs?
[13:12] Priya: yes TTLs and prefix caching per-route, also soft-locks during rollouts so we don't evict mid-request, slight transcription: soft locks -> soft-locks, sorry

[18:00] Priya: quantization tradeoffs: INT8 gives ~1.8-2x throughput improvement with small hit on perplexity vs FP16; for Qwen architectures we see larger accuracy drop at 4-bit unless we do per-layer mixed quantization. We push QAT for customer-critical flows.
[18:40] Dana: do you recommend our small hallucination-sensitive tasks use FP16 only?
[18:45] Priya: yes, for high-fidelity tasks we recommend FP16 or hybrid INT8 per-layer; for bulk chat logs INT8 is fine

[24:00] Alex: MoE routing - Luis can you explain your current setup?
[24:08] Luis: right now we have a 32-expert MoE with dynamic routing, but when traffic spikes routing decisions are expensive and we see memory thrash
[24:18] Priya: right, routing cost is twofold: compute overhead per token (gating network) and memory movement to pull expert weights/activations. For sparse MoE models on GPUs, it's often cheaper to overprovision expert capacity than to shuffle between devices in real time
[25:00] Priya: numbers: in our tests a single token routing step added ~2-4ms per token at 1k tokens/sec on 8-GPU cluster, but if you include expert transfer it's more like 8-12ms depending on interconnect
[25:40] Marco: interconnect matters, rdma/ib gives better perf than tcp, if you're on-prem check your switch fabric

[32:00] Priya: rope scaling - longer context with RoPE requires careful scaling of rotary frequencies; without scaling Qwen style models can hallucinate or degrade on long contexts
[32:30] Dana: we've seen ~3-6% drop in seq2seq accuracy after 8k tokens
[32:45] Priya: yes, we recommend exrapolation-friendly rope configs: scale down rotary frequencies for higher layers, do training-time rope deltas, and evaluate extrapolation at inference using held-out prompts

[40:00] Alex: can you talk about kernel selection and compilation?
[40:06] Priya: our runtime picks kernels based on model shape/sequence length. For Qwen with long sequences we select fused attention and rotary kernels; for Mistral we pick grouped linear kernels to save memory. Compilation step adds a warmup cost (seconds) but once compiled runtime is faster
[41:00] Dana: are these precompiled for hosted? For on-prem do we need to run our own compilation?
[41:08] Priya: hosted has precompiled kernel sets for common hw; on-prem we run compilation at deploy time, that's why we ask for representative sequence length distribution

[48:00] Luis: networking/KMS for VPCs - how do you handle KMS/HSM in private deployments?
[48:10] Marco: we integrate with customer KMS via peered VPN or private link, support on-prem HSM via PKCS#11, we stream audit logs to your SIEM, note sometimes we have intermittent auth latencies depending on KMS throughput
[48:45] Rachel: any compliance impacts for quantized models storing cache? do we store user content in KV cache?
[48:52] Alex: by default KV cache is ephemeral and encrypted; for enterprise we can turn off persistent logs, we also support SSE-KMS and customer-managed keys

[55:00] Priya: on batching strategies: adaptive batching windows using latency SLOs, token-aware batching for low-variance flows, and request shaping for steady throughput. Example: for 600 qps target we'd set max batch 16 with 15ms window for p95 ~150ms on a dedicated pod
[55:40] Dana: what's the memory impact of batch16 on Llama 70B?
[55:46] Priya: high; you'd need NVMe+gpu memory offload strategies or quantization to fit. With INT8 and offload we can get it to fit but there's CPU overhead

[63:00] Alex: recap and next steps
[63:10] Dana: run your proposed 1k-request benchmark with our prompt set, we want p95 <200ms and budget constraints
[63:20] Alex: we'll run benchmarks both hosted and a dedicated config, Priya will send quant spreadsheet, Marco will detail network/KMS setup
[63:35] Rachel: timeline: if benchmarks look good we want pilot in Dec, we're ready to sign an MoU after security review

[70:00] Priya: quick note - for MoE if you can't commit to overprovisioning we recommend gating + expert pruning to reduce swap
[70:20] Luis: understood
[71:00] Alex: thanks all, sending meeting notes and action items, will follow up with SOW and security pack
[71:10] Dana: thanks
[71:12] [END]
